name: Poland
tagline: A country that was erased from the map for 123 years and rebuilt its capital from paintings.
summary: Poland is large, flat in the middle, mountainous in the south and forested in the east, where Europe's last primeval woodland still stands. Its cities carry the twentieth century openly: Warsaw was destroyed and reconstructed, Kraków survived intact, Gdańsk was rebuilt as a Hanseatic port. It is one of the best-value countries in Europe and the food has become genuinely interesting in the last decade.

season.note: Summer for the lakes, the coast and the Tatras. September is warm and empty. Winter is properly cold and Kraków's Christmas market is one of the oldest in Europe.

getting_around: Intercity trains between the main cities are fast and cheap; regional services are slow but reach everywhere. FlixBus and domestic operators fill the gaps. Kraków, Wrocław and Gdańsk are all walkable.
food: Pierogi, boiled or fried, in a dozen fillings and never just one
Żurek: sour rye soup with sausage and egg, served in bread
Vodka, which is a category here rather than a drink

festivals.name: Wianki, midsummer wreaths on the Vistula

know: Auschwitz-Birkenau is a memorial and a cemetery; visits are free, timed, and behaviour there matters.
Milk bars (bar mleczny) are subsidised canteens serving a full meal for a few euros.
The złoty, not the euro, though cards work nearly everywhere.

regions.name: Lesser Poland & the South
regions.summary: Kraków, the salt mine, the memorial at Oświęcim, and the Tatra mountains beyond.

cities.name: Kraków
cities.summary: The royal capital that survived the war, with Europe's largest medieval square and a Jewish quarter that is now a district again.
highlights: The Rynek and the hourly trumpet call that stops mid-note
Wawel castle and cathedral, where Polish kings are buried
Kazimierz: synagogues, bars and Schindler's factory museum
Wieliczka's salt mine, carved into chapels 135 metres down

experiences.name: Lunch in a milk bar
experiences.summary: A communist-era subsidised canteen, still running, still cheap; queue, point, pay, and eat what Poland actually eats.

experiences.name: The salt cathedral at Wieliczka
experiences.summary: A chapel 101 metres underground with chandeliers of salt crystal, carved by miners over decades in their own time.

cities.name: Zakopane & the Tatras
cities.summary: A wooden mountain town under the only alpine range in Poland, with its own architectural style.
highlights: Morskie Oko, a lake under a wall of granite
The Zakopane style — timber villas designed as a national architecture
Oscypek, smoked sheep cheese, grilled and sold from carts

experiences.name: The walk to Morskie Oko
experiences.summary: Nine kilometres of asphalt road that everyone does, then a steep hour above it that almost nobody does — take the second part.

regions.name: Masovia & the Centre
regions.summary: The rebuilt capital, and the low country of the Vistula around it.

cities.name: Warsaw
cities.summary: Eighty-five per cent destroyed in 1944 and rebuilt from Canaletto's paintings, with a Stalinist tower and glass towers around it.
highlights: POLIN, the museum of a thousand years of Polish Jews
The Warsaw Rising Museum, loud and unsparing
The reconstructed Old Town, itself a UNESCO site for how it was rebuilt
Chopin concerts in Łazienki park on summer Sundays

experiences.name: POLIN, a thousand years
experiences.summary: The museum deliberately spends most of its space on Jewish life rather than its destruction, which is what makes it unlike any other.

regions.name: Pomerania & the East
regions.summary: The Baltic coast and Gdańsk, and the primeval forest on the Belarusian border.

cities.name: Gdańsk
cities.summary: A Hanseatic port of narrow gabled houses, where the war began and Solidarity ended it.
highlights: Długi Targ and the crane on the waterfront
The European Solidarity Centre at the shipyard gate
Westerplatte, where the first shots of 1939 were fired
Amber, worked here for a thousand years

cities.name: Białowieża
cities.summary: The last primeval lowland forest in Europe, with wild bison in it, on the Belarusian border.
highlights: The strict reserve, entered only with a licensed guide
European bison — some 600 of them, wild
Trees that have never been felled, some 400 years old

experiences.name: Bison at first light
experiences.summary: A guide, a hide and a 4 am start; the forest's edge meadows are where the herds actually come out.
